Returns read-only facts about this machine as one plain object.

Uptime, OS and build, IPv4, fixed disks, last installed update, Defender and BitLocker state, and the console user. Every probe is read-only and fails on its own: a missing WMI class, a timeout or a lack of elevation leaves that field Unknown or empty instead of failing the wallpaper.
The object is plain data. Replace it with your own function that returns the same property names and the presentation code keeps working.

command:example.maml:title: EXAMPLE 1
command:example.dev:code: $facts = Get-BGInfoSystemInfo New-BGInfoValue -Name 'Uptime' -Value $facts.UptimeText $facts.Disks | New-BGInfoTable -Title 'Disks' -Property Drive, FreeGB, UsedPercent

Runs your data-collection code with a time limit and a fallback value.

A wallpaper must never fail or hang at logon because one source is slow or down. The script block runs in its own runspace; when it throws, returns nothing or exceeds -TimeoutSeconds, the cmdlet writes a warning and returns -Default instead.
Variables of the calling script are not visible inside the script block. Pass what it needs with -ArgumentList and read it with param().
